topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: The Nature and Biological Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explain how endogenous cellular errors and inherited predispositions drive the accumulation of oncogenic mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and the 'Bad Luck' Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore suspected environmental carcinogens and evaluate epidemiological evidence and scientific debate regarding whether cancer is primarily driven by preventable exposures or random bad luck.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Causes of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, focusing in detail on the cooperative mechanisms driving Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mutagenic Mechanisms of Environmental Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms through which environmental mutagens damage DNA, either directly or following metabolic activation into reactive derivatives.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental stages cooperate with mutational events to drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the laboratory and epidemiological methodologies used to detect mutational signatures and evaluate whether environmental exposures are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer risks and reflections on balancing risk against practical benefits in everyday life.
